items.title: White House Threatens Congress, Saying Aggressive Investigations Could Be Crime
items.summary: As Democrats prepared to begin oversight inquiries, it was not clear what legal basis could support the threat. The Constitution grants lawmakers immunity for legislative acts.

items.title: Incoming House Intelligence Chairman Vows Oversight of CIA’s Use of Covert Action
items.summary: Representative Jim Himes, who will run the powerful intelligence committee in the new Congress, said he also planned to scrutinize contractor donations to President Trump’s construction projects.

items.title: Nvidia Scandal Unveils a Fierce Spy War Raging Behind Trump and Xi’s Diplomacy
items.summary: That the United States suspected Nvidia’s leader was a Chinese spy target underscores the deep distrust between the two powers, even as their leaders try to stabilize ties.

items.title: How a Suspected Chinese Spy Gained Access to Nvidia Chips
items.summary: A woman whom U.S. intelligence identified as a Chinese spy had ties to Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, dating to at least 2023. Ana Swanson, our reporter on trade and economics, explains what new photos show.

items.title: Nvidia Scandal Puts Lori Huang, Jensen Huang’s Wife, In the Spotlight
items.summary: Lori Huang, who has been married to the Nvidia chief executive for more than 40 years, stands out among tech titan spouses for how private she has been.

items.title: Silicon Valley Tech Allies Support Jensen Huang
items.summary: Elon Musk and other Silicon Valley figures cast the Nvidia chief’s relationship with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy as a personal lapse, not a security failure.

items.title: U.S. Efforts to Tighten Blockade of Iran Rely on Reluctant Neighbors
items.summary: Washington wants to intensify its economic pressure campaign on Iran by closing its land borders. Neighboring states, fearing economic fallout, are pushing back.

items.title: The S.S. United States, a Historic Supership, Heads to the Ocean Floor
items.summary: The 20th-century ocean liner will become an artificial reef, ending efforts to save a ship that was fast, luxurious and (almost) indestructible.

items.title: Recalling the S.S. United States as It Becomes a Florida Reef
items.summary: A New York Times editor has had a lifelong connection to the S.S. United States, which is becoming an artificial reef off the Florida coast.

items.title: The Fed Has to Raise Rates. How Fast to Go Has Officials Divided.
items.summary: The Federal Reserve’s gradual approach to raising rates is being tested by intensifying price pressures.

items.title: Greetings from Senegal, where breakdancers are competing in the Youth Olympics
items.summary: Senegal's breakdancers have been practicing for their country's historic hosting of the Youth Olympic Games this month. It's the first time Africa is hosting an Olympic event.

items.title: Kennedy relatives join the fight against Trump's arch, alleging harm to JFK's grave
items.summary: Nine members of the Kennedy family have joined the legal fight against Trump's D.C. arch, arguing it would disrupt views and cast shadows over their ancestors' graves at Arlington National Cemetery.

items.title: What's behind Democratic Socialists' historic victories in the midterms?
items.summary: Historian and The New Yorker writer Jill Lepore says the DSA, once maligned, is no longer "beyond the political pale." She discusses the history of socialism in America, and its current resurgence.

items.title: Following big Democratic wins, these swing voters are looking for results
items.summary: For the swing voters NPR is regularly checking in with as part of its Swing Shift series, the election results brought mixed emotions, as does the pending Democratic control of Congress.

items.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to a prisoner exchange as talks end with no big breakthrough
items.summary: Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a large exchange of prisoners of war. U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi led to this decision, marking the biggest humanitarian release since the war began in 2022.

items.title: House effectively ends Hegseth impeachment. And, 3 men accused of plotting U.K. attacks
items.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has been spared from the House's impeachment effort, at least for now. And, federal prosecutors arrested three men accused of being Iran-backed operatives.

items.title: An Iran-backed trio is accused of plotting attacks on a U.K. base hosting U.S. jets
items.summary: Iran-backed operatives have been charged over nearly 20 attacks, including a plot on a U.K. base housing U.S. troops. Separately, a U.S. soldier is held in the U.K. on Russia spying claims.

items.title: Morning News Brief: Hegseth impeachment, new House GOP leader, UK probes base plot
items.summary: Republicans block Hegseth impeachment, Trump ally picked to lead House GOP minority, UK investigates alleged Iran-backed plot.

items.title: Both sides now? Critics slam DOJ moves to dismiss convictions of Trump allies
items.summary: The DOJ moved to dismiss criminal convictions of former Trump adviser Steve Bannon and of the Oath Keepers, in what it calls "the interests of justice." Critics are crying foul.

items.title: Volunteer musicians play songs for veterans who are hospitalized
items.summary: Volunteer musicians play for veterans and others who are hospitalized. They're part of Musicians On Call, a group that spreads the healing power of music.

items.title: Route 66 turns 100. Here are five must-see spots along the road.
items.summary: Photographer Matt McClain shares memorable images from his journey marking the centennial.

items.title: Most transgender people have no regrets years after hormone therapy, study says
items.summary: The study, conducted by researchers in Texas, is the largest yet to examine satisfaction and regret in people who transitioned before they reached adulthood.

items.title: What to do if you, or someone around you, might be having a heart attack
items.summary: Heart attacks are more common in the winter months. Here's how to recognize the symptoms, and the best ways to respond.

items.title: ‘In Flanders Fields’: How a patriotic poem became an anti-war anthem
items.summary: Written by a Canadian soldier as a call to arms, it's now often excerpted to convey the futility of war.

items.title: A distress call, a flight tracker and the rush to explain a Learjet crash
items.summary: The fatal accident in Florida last week shows the fallout from a modern flood of data.

items.title: DHS watchdog will probe ICE’s compliance with wearing body cams
items.summary: In several shootings, federal immigration officers were not equipped with body cameras or did not have them turned on.

items.title: Meghan Markle’s estranged father jailed after allegedly removing ankle monitor
items.summary: Thomas Wayne Markle Sr., 82, charged last week with possession of child pornography, had been under house arrest in Lakeland, Florida.

items.title: Supreme Court grapples with arguments over federal agencies’ power to impose fines
items.summary: The case comes as the high court’s conservative majority has pared back the power of federal regulators. But even some conservatives appeared skeptical of going further.

items.title: Police chief defends timing of N.J. township’s wire-fraud announcement
items.summary: “If we tipped our hand too early, they could have liquidated everything,” Cranbury Township Police Chief Giuseppe N. DeChiara said of the $26 million theft, which remains under investigation.

items.title: Massachusetts State Police to pay Karen Read $100,000 settlement
items.summary: The Massachusetts State Police said the settlement would “avoid prolonged litigation and the significant costs to taxpayers of continuing the case.”
